canonical_name: Bogomolov conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties (Ullmo-Zhang theorem)
canonical_statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field, let L be an ample symmetric line bundle with associated canonical height, and let X be a closed geometrically integral subvariety of A. The points of X of arbitrarily small canonical height are Zariski dense in X if and only if X is a translate of an abelian subvariety by a torsion point.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: number field K; abelian variety A/K; ample symmetric line bundle L; closed geometrically integral subvariety X of A; exact Lean universes open
quantifiers: L : ample symmetric line bundle on A
X : closed geometrically integral subvariety of A
hypotheses: the height is the Neron-Tate canonical height associated to L
conclusion: Small-height points are Zariski dense in X if and only if X is a torsion translate of an abelian subvariety of A.

alternate_encodings.target: There exists epsilon > 0 such that the points of height <= epsilon are not Zariski dense whenever X is non-special
The essential minimum of X is zero if and only if X is special

excluded_degenerate_cases: Empty/non-geometrically-integral loci, nonsymmetric or nonample height data, and other conjectures bearing Bogomolov's name are outside the root. Zero-dimensional and X=A boundary behavior must be mutation-tested in the statement phase.
